title: Fan-in pattern: merging several channels into one

videos.script: Lesson 13 sent one stream to many goroutines. This lesson goes the other way: many channels, one loop. {{merge}} You build a merge. One goroutine copies each input onto a shared output. Three sources speak at different rates, and main reads them all from one channel, in the order they arrive. {{select}} Then a merge with select, in a single goroutine. It has a trap. A closed channel is always ready, so a careless loop receives almost a million zeros in a tenth of a second. Setting the channel to nil switches its case off. {{close}} Last, the question that decides it all: when to close the output. Too early, and a copier sends on a closed channel and the program panics. Never, and the reader waits for ever. The rule is that the last sender closes, and only something that counts the senders knows which one is last. {{end}} Lesson 15 chains these pieces into a pipeline.
